# rust.clippy passes on warnings unless flags deny them, rust.fmt-check
# fails on unformatted code, and rust.fmt formats it in place.
[!exec:cargo] skip

bit lax
stdout 'lax ▶ cargo clippy$'
stdout 'lax │ warning: writing `&Vec` instead of `&\[_\]`'
stdout 'lax ✔ ok'

! bit strict
stdout 'strict ▶ cargo clippy -- -D warnings$'
stdout 'strict │ error: writing `&Vec` instead of `&\[_\]`'
stderr 'test target ''strict'' failed'

! bit check
stdout 'check ▶ cargo fmt --check$'
stdout 'check │ Diff in .*src/lib\.rs'
stderr 'test target ''check'' failed'

bit fmt
stdout 'fmt ▶ cargo fmt$'
stdout 'fmt ✔ ok'
cmp src/lib.rs formatted.rs
bit fmt
stdout 'fmt · no changes'
bit check
stdout 'check ✔ ok'

# The runner's cp keeps the file's older mtime on macOS, which cargo reads as
# unchanged, so the system cp writes the fix.
exec cp fixed.rs src/lib.rs
bit strict
stdout 'strict ✔ ok'

-- BUILD.bit --
explicit lax = rust.clippy {}

explicit strict = rust.clippy {
  flags = ["--", "-D", "warnings"]
}

explicit fmt = rust.fmt {}

explicit check = rust.fmt-check {}
-- Cargo.toml --
[package]
name = "lint"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
-- src/lib.rs --
pub fn f(x: &Vec<i32>) -> usize {
    x.len()
}

pub fn  g( )->i32{1}
-- formatted.rs --
pub fn f(x: &Vec<i32>) -> usize {
    x.len()
}

pub fn g() -> i32 {
    1
}
-- fixed.rs --
pub fn f(x: &[i32]) -> usize {
    x.len()
}

pub fn g() -> i32 {
    1
}
